exclusions.reason: Admission rejection depends on process memory and listener acceptance, outside an immutable MySQL byte trace.
The live max-connections gate executes before a session and packet stream exist.
Backend selection, retry, abandonment, and rehydration require router and control-plane actors rather than one wire trace.
Public endpoint and cluster classification require listener, PROXY address, CIDR, and dial context.
Atomic configuration generation and listener reload behavior are exercised by control-protocol and runtime-config tests.
Configuration validation runs before admission and has no MySQL packet representation.

The optional restart-pinned observer socket and joined task ownership require real configuration and process lifecycle; validated by the control-config/tiproxy-rs tests and controlplane-cproute-recorder-evidence, outside a MySQL byte trace.

The restart-pinned metrics-owner port (zero selects an ephemeral port; an explicit port must fit uint16 and differ from every SQL listener and the API port; a Rust reload cannot replace it) is configuration validation and process startup behavior with no MySQL packet representation; validated by lib/config/proxy_test.go:TestMetricsOwnerPortIsExplicitRestartPinnedAndCollisionFree and rust/crates/control-config/tests/source.rs:metrics_owner_port_is_explicit_restart_pinned_and_collision_free.
The v1 oracle stores uncompressed MySQL frames; zlib negotiation and framing use Go golden vectors and compressed session tests.
Compressed sequence, reset, peek, discard, flush, and corrupt-frame semantics use the dedicated compression vector/runtime suites.
SQL traffic capture and replay are intentionally excluded from the Rust dataplane and must never enter this corpus.

EXCLUDED by the RUST_ROUTE_OWNER production boundary: Rust mode rejects custom Go HandshakeHandler implementations before listeners open, while the supported default handler never approves RECONNECT. The pure relay reference transition remains unit-tested; initial dial retry and candidate retirement are covered by ADM-003.
Direct backend authentication is a replay/test topology path and remains outside ordinary proxy-session corpus coverage.
Exact capability advertisement and masking are locked by handshake/runtime tests; existing corpus cases cover negotiated subsets only.
The current Go oracle has no malformed backend-greeting vector; retain this exclusion until that source gap is filled.
Frontend keepalive requires operating-system socket options and cannot be represented as MySQL records.
Backend keepalive transitions require a live health feed and socket owner.
Idle peer probing requires socket EOF and concurrency with the session loop, covered by runtime tests.
Coordinated stop-accept, safe drain, and force deadlines require listener and process lifecycle orchestration.
Force-close interruption and idempotent teardown require concurrent live I/O rather than sequential corpus records.
Close-time redirect reporting, hook notification, socket release, and route unregistering require control-plane ownership.
Managed-task panic recovery and cancellation are process supervision behavior.
Lifecycle quit-source attribution spans transport and control failures; focused observability/runtime tests are authoritative.
Asynchronous redirect serialization and once-only callbacks require control commands and two backend owners.
Candidate TLS, PROXY, compression, token authentication, restore, and atomic swap require a second live backend.
Held-BEGIN and internal-COMMIT ordering require an armed redirect and old/new backend interaction.
Candidate failure preservation and old-backend disconnect classification require two independently failing sockets.
Successful swap accounting, counter reset, keepalive, hooks, and stable frontend identity require live ownership transfer.
Keyspace-stable redirect refusal lives at the Go router issuance boundary before any Rust packet stream.

Actual Go lifecycle witnesses, bounded loss and independent Rust comparison require router owners and a live UDS consumer; controlplane-cproute-recorder-evidence supplies these checks, which an immutable MySQL byte stream cannot represent.
Raw socket byte and physical-packet accounting are validated at CountedIo and live session seams, not normalized trace payloads.
Durable per-keyspace/public/cross-AZ metering requires immutable attribution, migration, WAL, ACK, and the Go meter sink.
Prometheus command, handshake, lifetime, connection, and error-source labels are checked by observability integration tests.
Migration pending/success/failure metrics and backend gauges are Go control-plane observations of Rust lifecycle events.
Payload-free lifecycle log fields depend on connection, listener, namespace, backend, and quit context unavailable in a byte trace.

Process-level observations with no client wire traffic: the two monitor families come from a wall-clock sampling loop, and the rest read health, election and balancer state. An immutable MySQL byte trace cannot produce or observe them. Verification is the clock-driven monitor unit test, the Go promhttp oracle over native-families.json, and the startup-rollback test that the monitor is stopped and joined; ten of the twelve families are not implemented yet.
Buffer sizing, pooling, direct writes, counters, flush behavior, and post-TLS bounds require concrete I/O implementations.
SSLRequest-to-HandshakeResponse capability reconciliation crosses the transport upgrade boundary and needs a live TLS session.
Backend TLS enforcement, certificate cloning, and SNI require a selected backend and TLS transport.
TLS policy, identity, and certificate rotation are configuration and filesystem lifecycle behavior.
Multi-address/range listener binding and coordinated stop require operating-system listeners.
Namespace routing and dynamic topology stability require the Go router projection and live admissions.
Named backend-cluster isolation and legacy PD fallback are configuration/topology behavior before packet forwarding.

Backend connection counts are process state, not client wire traffic: an immutable MySQL byte trace can neither produce nor observe how many sessions a router incarnation physically owns. Verification is the ledger test that the count follows Go's connList exactly (reservation excluded, source kept until a migration succeeds, closed once), the Go promhttp oracle over native-families.json, and the comparator case pinning the one declared deviation for backend addresses shared between namespaces.

A health-check cycle duration is observer-loop timing, not client wire traffic: an immutable MySQL byte trace neither drives the probe round nor observes how long it took. Verification is the topology test that the gauge is written on every completed round including one that applied no verdict, plus the Go promhttp oracle over native-families.json. The declared deviation -- the Rust interval spans the probe round alone because discovery is a separate ticker -- is recorded in the parity row itself; it is a difference in what the interval covers, which no corpus trace could express.

The post-purge pending_migrate offset is an interaction between retention purge and in-flight migrations held in process state, with no MySQL packet representation. Verification is the control-router test that retiring a backend deletes its series without disturbing the ledger, and the Go-side reproduction of the offset rule; Rust reads the true in-flight count from the ledger and carries no offset, which is exactly the declared deviation and therefore not something a shared byte trace could compare.

server_owner reports which etcd elections this process holds. It is control-plane campaign state with no client wire traffic: a MySQL trace cannot win, hold or retire an election. Verification is the topology test deriving the label from the same key the campaign runs on across all four Go key shapes, the retirement test that the child is deleted rather than zeroed, and the Go oracle exercising a won-then-retired election. The declared gap -- only metric_reader elections exist because Rust has no VIP manager -- is a missing subsystem, not a metric difference.

This is an internal concurrency invariant, not an exposition property: a metric write made under a routing generation must not land after that generation is revoked. It has no MySQL byte representation at all -- the observable output is identical whether or not the fence exists, and only the interleaving differs. Verification is the CommitPermit ordering tests (both orders, barrier-pinned), the per-step owner/readiness/config/topology receipts, and the real-router regression that holds a scoring round between evaluation and commit while another thread publishes a new configuration.
